name: blank?
syntax: Input.blank? * Input - An input datapill. It can be a string, number, date, datetime, boolean, array, or object datatype.
description: Checks whether the input is considered blank according to Ruby conventions. This includes:

name: is_not_true?
syntax: Input.is_not_true? * Input - An input boolean, an integer (1 or 0), or an accepted string value.
description: Evaluates a boolean value and returns true if the evaluated value is not true.

name: is_true?
syntax: Input.is_true? * Input - An input boolean, an integer (1 or 0), or an accepted string value.
description: Evaluates a boolean value and returns true if the evaluated value is true.

name: present?
syntax: Input.present? * Input - An input datapill. It can be a string, number, date, or list datatype.
description: This formula will check the input and if there is a value present, it will return true. If the input is nil, boolean false, an empty string, or an empty list, the formula will return false.

name: presence
syntax: Input.presence * Input - An input datapill. It can be a string, number, date, or datetime datatype.
description: Returns the data if it exists, returns nil if it does not.

name: include?
syntax: Input.include?(substring) * Input - A string input. * substring - The substring to check for.
description: Checks if the string contains a specific substring. Returns true if it does.

name: exclude?
syntax: Input.exclude?(substring) * Input - A string input. * substring - The substring to check for.
description: Checks if the string contains a specific substring. Returns false if it does.

name: match?
syntax: Input.match?(pattern) * Input - A string input. * pattern - The regex pattern to check for.
description: Checks if the string contains a specific regular expression (regex) pattern. Returns true if it does.

name: ends_with?
syntax: Input.ends_with?(substring) * Input - A string input. * substring - The substring to check for.
description: Checks if the string ends with a specific substring. Returns true if it does.

name: starts_with?
syntax: Input.starts_with?(substring) * Input - A string input. * substring - The substring to check for.
description: Checks if the string starts with a specific substring. Returns true if it does.

name: parameterize
syntax: Input.parameterize * Input - An input string.
description: Replaces special characters in a string with standard characters. Used when app does not accept non-standard characters.

name: lstrip
syntax: String.lstrip * String - An input string.
description: This formula removes the white space at the beginning of the input string.

name: rstrip
syntax: String.rstrip * String - An input string.
description: This formula removes the white space at the end of the input string.

name: scrub
syntax: String.scrub(replacement string) * String - An input string.
description: If the string is an invalid byte sequence, the formula replaces the invalid bytes with a replacement character. If the string is not invalid, the formula returns the original string.

name: strip
syntax: String.strip * String - An input string.
description: This formula removes the white space at the beginning and end of the input string.

name: strip_tags
syntax: String.strip_tags * String - An input string.
description: This formula removes HTML tags embedded in a string.

name: ljust
syntax: String.ljust(length,character) * String - An input string. * length - The length of the output string. * character - (optional) The character or string used to pad the input string. If unspecified, the default pad character is a blank space.
description: Aligns the string to left and pads it with whitespace or the provided character/string until the string is a specified length.

name: rjust
syntax: String.rjust(length,character) * String - An input string. * length - The length of the output string. * character - (optional) The character or string padding the input string. If unspecified, the default pad character is a blank space.
description: Aligns the string to left and pads it with whitespace or a provided character/string until string is a specified length.

name: reverse
syntax: String.reverse * String - An input string.
description: Inverts a string, reordering the characters in reverse order. Case is preserved.

name: gsub
syntax: String.gsub(find,replace) * String - An input string. You can use a datapill or a static string value. * find - The string or regular expression (regex) to look for. Use a /pattern/ syntax for regex. * replace - The replacement string. You can define the replacement using a string or [hash](/en/formulas/array-list-formulas.md#hashes).
description: Replace parts of a text string. Returns a new string with the replaced characters.

name: sub
syntax: String.sub(find,replace) * String - An input string. You can use a datapill or a static string value. * find - The string or regular expression (regex) to look for. Use a /pattern/ syntax for regex. * replace - The replacement string. You can define the replacement using a string or [hash](/en/formulas/array-list-formulas.md#hashes).
description: Replaces the first occurrence of the first input value, with the second input value, within the string. This formula is case-sensitive - make sure to type in uppercase or lowercase before comparison if you are concerned about case sensitivity.

name: length
syntax: String.length * String - An input string.
description: Returns the number of characters within an input string, including whitespaces.

name: slice
syntax: String.slice(start,end) * String - An input string. * start - The index of the string to start returning a partial segment at. Strings are zero-indexed. * end - (optional) The number of characters to return. If unspecified, the formula will return only one character.
description: Returns a partial segment of a string.

name: scan
syntax: String.scan(pattern) * String - An input string. * regex pattern - The regex pattern to search for.
description: Scan the string for the regex pattern to retrieve and returns an array.

name: encode
syntax: String.encode(encoding) * String - An input string. * encoding - Name of the encoding (for example, Windows-1252). Refer to the [Ruby Programming/Encoding](https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Ruby_Programming/Encoding) Wikibooks article for more information on ruby encodings.
description: Returns the string encoded.

name: transliterate
syntax: String.transliterate * String - An input string.
description: Replaces non-ASCII characters with an ASCII approximation. If no approximation exists, it uses a replacement character which defaults to '?'.

name: capitalize
syntax: String.capitalize * String - An input string.
description: Converts the input string into sentence case, where the first character of the string is capitalized and all other characters are lowercase.

name: titleize
syntax: String.titleize * String - An input string.
description: Converts the input string into title case, where the first character of each word is capitalized and all other characters are lowercase.

name: upcase
syntax: String.upcase * String - An input string.
description: Convert text to uppercase.

name: downcase
syntax: String.downcase * String - An input string.
description: Convert text to lowercase.

name: quote
syntax: String.quote * String - An input string.
description: Quotes a string, escaping any ' (single quote) characters

name: split
syntax: String.split(char) * String - An input string value. You can use a datapill or a static value. * char - (optional) The character to split the text at. This is case sensitive. If no character is defined, then by default, strings are split by white spaces.
description: This formula divides a string around a specified character and returns an array of strings.

name: bytes
syntax: String.bytes * String - An input string.
description: Returns an array of bytes for a given string.

name: bytesize
syntax: Input.bytesize * Input - Any input string.
description: Returns the length of a given string in bytes.

name: byteslice
syntax: Input.byteslice(0,4) * Input - Any input string.
description: Returns a substring of specified bytes instead of length. In some cases, non ASCII characters such as Japanese or Chinese may use multiple bytes.

name: ordinalize

name: to_i

description: Converts data to an integer (whole number) datatype.

name: The add (+) operator
description: This operator allows the addition of operands on either side. This section talks about number arithmetic. Refer to [Date arithmetic](/en/formulas/date-formulas.md#date-arithmetic) for more information on date-specific arithmetic.

name: The subtract (-) operator
description: This operator subtracts the right hand operand from the left hand operand. This section talks about number arithmetic. Refer to [Date arithmetic](/en/formulas/date-formulas.md#date-arithmetic) for more information on date-specific arithmetic.

name: The multiply (\*) operator
description: This operator multiplies the operands on either side.

name: The divide (/) operator
description: Divides left hand operand by right hand operand.

name: The exponential (\*\*) operator
description: Left hand operand to the power of the right hand operand.

name: The modulo (%) operator
description: Divides left hand operand by right hand operand and returns the remainder.

name: first
syntax: List.first(number) * List - An input list. * number - (optional) The number of items to retrieve from the list. If not specified, the formula will return only *one* item.
description: This formula returns the first item in a list.

name: last
syntax: List.last(number) * List - An input list. * number - (optional) The number of items to retrieve from the list. If not specified, the formula will return only *one* item.
description: This formula returns the last item in a list.

name: index
syntax: Input.index(value) * Input - An input list. * value - The value to search for in the list.
description: Returns the index of the first item matching the given value. Returns nil if no matching items are found.

name: count
syntax: List.count * List - An input of list datatype.
description: Returns the number of items in a list.

name: where
description: Retrieves only the rows (hashes) which satisfy the specified WHERE condition. This formula accepts a single argument in the form of a hash with one or more key-value pairs.

name: except
description: Returns a hash that includes everything except given keys.

name: pluck
description: Retrieves only the columns which have been specified.

name: format_map
description: Creates a new array of strings by applying a format to each item in the input array. You can reference input values in the format string using %{field_name} for hashes, or %s for sub-arrays and scalar values.

name: join
syntax: List.join(separator) * List - An input of list datatype. * separator - The character to add between items when they are joined. If no separator is specified, the list items will be joined together.
description: Combines all items in a list into a text string. A separator is placed between each item.

name: smart_join
syntax: List.smart_join(separator) * List - An input of list datatype. * separator - The character to add between items when they are joined. If no separator is specified, a blank space will be used as the joining character.
description: Joins list elements into a string. Removes empty and nil values and trims any white space before joining.

name: concat
syntax: List.concat(list_to_be_joined) * List - An input of list datatype. * list_to_be_joined - The other list to be concatenated with the original list input.
description: Concatenates 2 lists into a single list. Nested lists will NOT be flattened.

description: Reverses the order of a list.

name: sum

description: For integers and decimals, the numbers will be added together and the total sum obtained. For strings, the strings will be concatenated together to form a longer string.

name: uniq

description: Returns a list containing unique items.

name: flatten

name: length

description: Returns the number of elements in self. Returns 0 if the list is empty.

name: max
syntax: List.max * List - An input of list datatype.
description: Returns largest value in an array. When comparing numbers, the largest number is returned. When comparing strings, the string with the largest ASCII value is returned.

name: min

description: Returns smallest value in an array. When comparing numbers, the smallest number is returned. When comparing strings, the string with the smallest ASCII value is returned.
